https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/cap-ferre.text: Rebecca Robinson Updated Fri, 24 July 2026 at 11:17 am UTC 0 Firefighters trying to tackle the flames in Cap Ferret on July 23 (Image: AFP via Getty Images) A holiday hotspot has been evacuated by France's authorities as a horrifying wildfire continues to rage. Hundreds of people have been escaping the Cap Ferret peninsula in South-west France after the entire area was evacuated amid the terrifying blaze. They have been told to leave via the main road towards Bordeaux or take boats being made available between 7am and 10am local time from four piers. So far, boats have taken more than 400 people from Cap Ferret, which stretches along France's Atlantic coast to the west of Bordeaux. The fire has been raging since Tuesday. (Image: Getty) The region's prefect, Sophie Brocas, said the "final phase" of the evacuation began early on Friday morning. She said 10,000 visitors were evacuated overnight Wednesday, taking the total up to a whopping 20,000. The wildfire has raged in the Gironde region since Tuesday, where it began in Saumous and tore through 8,700 hectares overnight alone. It is now burning near the Arcachon Bay area - a tourist hotspot where many visitors are staying in campsites. Two firefighters were killed while tackling the blaze near Bordeaux Airport on Tuesday, though officials said there have been no new injuries as of Friday. Thousands of people have been forced to evacuate. (Image: Getty) Emmanuel Macron called the situation "very tense" and asked for help from the European Union . The French President said aircraft from Croatia, Portugal, the Czech Republic, and Slovakia will soon be mobilised to support the country. Gironde fire service chief Marc Vermeulen warned that rising temperatures and strong winds could exacerbate the situation. He said Thursday: "The work was relentless all night. It'll peak at 8pm. Then we'll have to deal with... highly variable winds so we're currently tackling a fire that is going to be difficult to predict and that's why we cannot relax our guard." https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/catego.text: River barges carrying goods pass near the Cernavoda Nuclear Power Plant along the Danube–Black Sea Canal in Cernavoda, Romania. (EPA Images pic) BUCHAREST: Levels on the Danube river around Romania's nuclear power plant will continue to fall this week, its water management agency said on Monday, despite urgent measures to re-direct cooling water to its sole working reactor. Record-low water levels on the Danube have already forced the shutdown of one of the EU country's two reactors, which normally account for 20% of all its power needs, and authorities have taken steps to ensure the other turbine kept running. Europe, the world's fastest-warming continent, has been ravaged by record-breaking heat and destructive wildfires this summer, with France and Spain scorched while Romania and Hungary had to cut their power output and rely on costly imports. Romania has blown up a rock obstruction, dredged the river bed and sunk four barges filled with rocks to create a dike and redirect flows towards the nuclear power plant in Cernavoda. The measures had lifted water levels around the reactor by 4cm (1.57 inches) on Sunday, Romania's energy ministry said, ensuring it could operate for a further nine days. But on Monday, the state water management agency said updated forecasts showed rain upstream would not make a difference for Romania, the last country through which the Danube flows before it enters the Black Sea. The agency said the level of the Danube at its Romanian entry point would remain at an all-time low for the next seven days, while levels around the plant would fall until August 16. In a statement it said it recommended authorities "continue to dredge the river bed in access areas to ensure water flows towards the plant in Cernavoda". Romania's government on Monday allotted additional funds to the transport ministry for dredging works to deepen the river bed on the branch where the reactor sits. Romania has already declared a state of energy emergency throughout August and asked companies and households to voluntarily reduce consumption during peak evening hours. Romania relies on a mix of gas, coal, hydro, nuclear and renewables for electricity generation but needs billions of euros in investment to replace ageing facilities and boost battery storage and grid interconnections.

https://www.politico.eu/article/macron-i.text: PARIS — President Emmanuel Macron has invited European heads of state to attend Pope Leo XIV’s address on the last day of his visit to France later this month, three European diplomats told POLITICO. The pontiff will deliver a speech titled “The roots of Europe, for peace and unity,” in the French northeastern city of Metz, on Sept. 28 . The event will be an “opportunity to celebrate the memory of Robert Schuman, father of Europe and declared venerable by Pope Francis in 2021,” the official invitation, seen by POLITICO, reads. Metz is the hometown of former French Prime Minister Robert Schuman, a founding father of the European Union and a practicing Catholic. Advertisement Advertisement The location “isn’t a usual [stop] of a papal visit,” said Archbishop Philippe Ballot of Metz in an interview with French weekly Le Point. “How coherent, though, when you dig deeper. On the last day of his trip, he opens up to Europe and the world,” he added. Le Point first reported the invitations . The pope will be in France for a four-day official visit from Sept. 25 to 28 and is to meet Macron at the Elysée Palace, visit Notre-Dame Cathedral and the Unesco headquarters, where he’s expected to talk about artificial intelligence. In his first major encyclical — an official letter the Pope writes to Catholic bishops — released in May, the pontiff has urged stronger AI regulation and warned against the spread of misinformation and the growing lack of human control. Pope Leo XIV’s trip will be the first official papal visit to France since Benedict XVI went to Paris and Lourdes in 2008.
